title: Lesson 4: Discovering Your Gifts
description: Jesus gave Apostles, Prophets, Evangelists, Shepherds, and Teachers to equip all His people for ministry. Through five farmers working one field, you will notice how God may have wired you to strengthen His Church.

blocks.text: Lessons 1, 2, and 3 walked outward through three connected homes: your neighbors next door, your family under your roof, and the church family God has given you. Now the question turns personal: What grace has God placed in me for the good of His people? Before the answer, a story about a field.

blocks.alt: A farmer standing in a wide field, tools at hand, ready for the work the field needs

blocks.title: The Five Farmers in the Field
blocks.text:
A master farmer owned a field full of possibility, but the field needed more than one kind of work. Some ground needed to be started from scratch. Some rows needed a careful watcher, some places needed seed, and some new plants needed water. Some branches needed pruning so the fruit could grow strong.

So the master farmer called five farmers and gave each one what the field would need: a plow, a watcher's eye on the sky, a seed bag, a watering can, and pruning shears. When each farmer used what had been given, the whole field changed. No single farmer could tend the whole field, but each one carried a grace the field needed.
That is the question underneath this lesson. What tool has the Master Farmer placed in your hands for the field He loves?
Equipped for the Work of Ministry

And he gave the apostles, the prophets, the evangelists, the shepherds and teachers, to equip the saints for the work of ministry, for building up the body of Christ, until we all attain to the unity of the faith and of the knowledge of the Son of God, to mature manhood, to the measure of the stature of the fullness of Christ.

This verse changes the way most people think about church. Jesus gave apostles, prophets, evangelists, shepherds, and teachers to equip the saints for the work of ministry. The gifts are not handed out so a few professionals can do the work while everyone else watches, but so that every believer is equipped and useful in the body. Saints means every person who belongs to Jesus, and ministry simply means serving in a way that builds others up: welcoming a newcomer, teaching a child, praying for a drifting friend, helping a new believer find their footing.

Hear the grace underneath before any of it becomes pressure. Paul does not say, "Earn your way onto the team." He says Jesus gave. Whatever gift God has placed in you, He put it there. Your job is to notice it, use it, and let Him build the body through you.
4.1 - What work in your church or community do you enjoy and seem good at?
Five Farmers, One Field

Paul's five words, often shortened to APEST, are not five ranks of clergy. They are five ways Jesus continues His own ministry through His people, and most believers carry a blend. Step through the five farmers and notice what each one sees, what each one cares about, and what kind of work makes the field come alive.

Each farmer notices something first. The Plower sees unopened ground and says, there is more field to cultivate. The Watcher sees drift, danger, and the person being overlooked. The Planter sees where seed can be scattered and who is curious about Jesus. The Waterer sees the tender and the tired. The Pruner sees confusion that needs clear, patient teaching. As you read them, ask: What do I notice first? What gives me holy energy? What do people already ask me to help with?
4.2 - Which of the five farmers are you most like, and what do you notice first in the field?
A Gift Is Grace, Not a Label

Having gifts that differ according to the grace given to us, let us use them: if prophecy, in proportion to our faith; if service, in our serving; the one who teaches, in his teaching; the one who exhorts, in his exhortation; the one who contributes, in generosity; the one who leads, with zeal; the one who does acts of mercy, with cheerfulness.

Notice the phrase according to the grace given to us. Your gift is grace. APEST is one helpful lens, and Romans 12 gives another list of ways grace shows up in the church. The point is the same: use what God has given you. Keep discerning by watching two things, what you notice first in the field and where your serving seems to strengthen others.

Jesus is the center of all five. He is the perfect Apostle, sent by the Father; the perfect Prophet, speaking the Father's heart; the perfect Evangelist, announcing good news; the perfect Shepherd, laying down His life for the sheep; and the perfect Teacher, opening the Scriptures. When Jesus gives gifts to His Church, He is sharing pieces of His own ministry with His people.
4.3 - What is one way you could use that gift in your church family this week?
This Week's Practice

Pick the farmer you sensed God may have made you, and pray a short prayer over it each morning this week. Thank God that this is a grace He gave, not a wage you earned. Then ask Him for one person, one moment, or one need where you can use it that day.
4.4 - Who in your church family do you see as one of the five farmers, and how could you tell them what you notice?
Lesson 4 Review

Jesus gave five kinds of gifts to His Church, Apostle, Prophet, Evangelist, Shepherd, and Teacher, to equip all His people for the work of ministry. Like five farmers tending one field, each one notices something different and brings something the field needs. Your gift is grace, not a label. Notice the tool the Master Farmer has placed in your hands, and start putting it to use.
In the next lesson, you will see what it looks like when faith is tested by suffering and trials.
Closing Reflections
What is one key thing you learned from this lesson?
What is one step you are going to take this week?
What is a prayer request for this week?
